ASLM vs Non-ASLM: How Much Tissue Are You Really Imaging at Once?

Keep the specimen and camera fixed. Change only the detection magnification and the illumination numerical aperture. The tool separates two jobs: detection magnification sets the field of view, while illumination NA sets the Gaussian confocal parameter. The ASLM comparison asks how many source acquisitions are required to build the same stitched Z plane.

Two optical variables

1 · Detection objective

Magnification determines specimen-side pixel scale and detector FOV.

2 · Illumination objective

Illumination NA determines Gaussian waist and confocal parameter. Higher NA produces a thinner waist but a shorter useful propagation length.
Two objectives, two jobs.
Detection magnification changes how much tissue lands on the camera. Illumination NA changes how far the thin Gaussian waist remains useful. ASLM sweeps that waist across the detector field instead of repeating discrete waist positions.

Teaching model. Detector FOV is calculated from camera pitch, active pixels and detection magnification. Gaussian waist and confocal parameter are calculated from effective illumination NA, wavelength and refractive index. The discrete-position count is a geometric coverage estimate, not a claim about a specific commercial implementation.
